question: Does any ink reader show an isolated short block of larger, spaced letterforms after the last text column of PHerc. Paris 4 (the innermost wraps), at any depth offset, that is absent in the reverse-depth and depth-shuffled controls?

inputs.surfaces: published PHercParis4 segments covering the innermost wraps after the last column (start with tracing 20260701183124-w010-027 if its mesh is public); spiral-input verified_patches only as geometry
inputs.reader: scrollprize/ink_9um hybrid_3d2d seed42 and seed43 step-075000 (SHA-256 in docs/logs/2026-10-07-w035-cpu.md), downsampled 2.4 um renders to about 9.6 um

readout_rule: Fixed before any map exists. Candidate region only if: (1) components of 1.5 to 6 mm height (larger than body text, about 2 to 3 mm) cluster in at most 4 rows; (2) the cluster lies past the last body column along the winding, separated by at least 10 mm of blank surface; (3) present on both seeds; (4) absent in reverse depth and in kit shuffle seed 0; (5) not inside any training label region. Anything else is reported as no candidate. Never a reading.
readout_rule_sha256: filled in by kit run init
villa_commit: git rev-parse HEAD of the villa checkout used

compute.where: pay-per-second serverless GPU (Modal A10 class), or the Mac M1 Pro MPS at zero cash cost
compute.estimate: render plus inference of about 30,000 mm2 at 13 depth offsets x 2 seeds x 2 directions: about 16 GPU hours. python3 -m kit cost --gpu-hours 16 --rate 1.10 gives $17.60; at --rate 0.60 gives $9.60. Egress free (AWS Open Data). Budget cap proposed: $25.
compute.approval: NOT launched. Needs the owner's budget decision (AGENTS.md standing decision on GPU rental).
